critique.evidence: The screen advances the defense story by translating measured simulation outcomes into attacker economics, showing before/after cost, success rate, observed successes, and ROI, while clearly stating that deterrence is unproven. It connects to the Mastercard brief through an authorization-time intent-signal proposal and explicitly labels it “proposed, not deployed,” with no live Mastercard or payment-network result claimed. However, it does not demonstrate that intent-integrity signals actually reach an authorization system, influence a decision, or produce a payment-network outcome; the displayed ROI also lacks visible provenance for fraud value and total attack-cost inputs.
critique.fix: Add a traceable demo artifact showing one signed intent mandate flowing into an issuer-style authorization decision, with the resulting approve/step-up/decline outcome and economics calculation linked to named simulation inputs. Keep the Mastercard integration explicitly simulated unless a real integration is proven.
